newsitem.title: THAILAND: ASEAN weighs option to steady volatile currencies.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN weighs option to steady volatile currencies.

text.p: Senior ASEAN finance ministry officials on Friday discussed reviving a regional currency stabilising instrument in the wake of recent volatility and the dollar's rise.
The officials were meeting in this resort island ahead of a one-day meeting of seven Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) finance ministers here on Saturday.
ASEAN groups Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Singapore, Brunei and Vietnam.

Chanchai Musinisakorn, a Thai finance ministry economist, told reporters that the senior officials weighed merits of reactivating, and possibly expanding, a $200 million ASEAN Swap Arrangement that had never been put to use since its creation in 1977.
Some ASEAN currencies, like the Thai baht, have been under pressure recently because of a sudden surge in the U.S. dollar.

Chanchai said that senior officials at their meeting did not reach a decision on whether or when to revive the currency stabilising tool but agreed that its original size needed to be expanded to make it effective.

He said any decision for ASEAN to revive the instrument would depend on the extent to which members of the regional grouping could tap alternative emergency funds from the $48 billion New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB) body of the International Monetary Fund.
The IMF executive board in late January approved the NAB, an emergency credit line to be used in situations that could threaten the stability of the world monetary system.

Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand are among 25 potential participants in the NAB which will enter into force when it has been adhered to by participants with credit arrangements amounting to no less than $41 billion.
